active_directory.notes: Domain Controller Security logs map well to Authentication and Change for privileged operations; replication and LDAP detail varies by collection method.

apm.notes: Distributed traces are high cardinality; mapping spans to CIM-style DMs is often partial—many fields stay in APM-native models.

app_servers.notes: JVM, .NET, and Node stacks differ; structured logging adoption drives parseability more than platform.

app_servers_nonprod.notes: Non-production app tiers often have verbose debug logging enabled; parseability still varies by stack.

application_event_log.notes: Third-party and .NET application providers register their own providers; without vendor-specific knowledge many events stay unparsed beyond raw message.

asset_cmdb.notes: CMDB snapshots and reconciliation jobs are batch or API pull dominated; treat as enrichment more than real-time security telemetry.

business_txn.notes: Mainframes, ERP, and payment switches expose very different schemas; business identifiers (order ID, claim number) are rarely CIM-standard.

casb.notes: API discovery and policy enforcement consoles emit vendor-specific scored events; correlation back to upstream SaaS IDs is the main integration effort.

config_mgmt.notes: Chef/Puppet/Ansible/SCCM drift and inventory deltas are change-centric; overlap with CMDB varies by enterprise automation maturity.

cspm.notes: Findings are often assessment-style records rather than streaming security logs; vendor-specific schemas rarely map 1:1 to Splunk CIM without custom extractions.

cwpp.notes: Workload agent telemetry overlaps EDR; compliance-oriented CWPP may emphasize misconfig and image vulnerability vs runtime process trees.

database.notes: Native audit vs agent-based interception vs gateway SQL logging varies widely; full text queries may be excluded for compliance.

db_access.notes: Gateway or native DB auditing of successful connections and object access; full SQL text capture is often excluded for compliance.

db_transaction.notes: Dedicated transaction/change-data feeds (CDC, redo/mining) are schema-heavy; many environments log only metadata or sampled statements.

ddos.notes: Scrubbing center and CDN mitigation signals are often aggregated; volumetric details may arrive as flow summaries not full packets.

deception.notes: Decoys and breadcrumbs generate sparse but high-fidelity engagement signals; alerting semantics differ from IDS correlation.

desktops.notes: Laptop fleets without uniform EDR/Sysmon resemble sparse windows_servers telemetry; SaaS client auditing may be the only signal for some user actions.

devops_cicd.notes: Pipeline run logs and SCM/Git audit events blend build telemetry with developer auth; secrets scanners add security-relevant findings.

dhcp.notes: Microsoft DHCP vs ISC/BIND vs IPAM integrations differ; IP lease telemetry aids asset correlation but is not a substitute for endpoint identity.

dhcp_server_logs.notes: Microsoft DHCP lease audit vs ISC logs; aids asset correlation but is not a substitute for endpoint or IdP identity.

dlp.notes: Endpoint vs network vs cloud DLP consoles emit different evidence types; content inspection depth affects privacy and retention policy.

dns.notes: Resolver and authoritative roles differ; passive DNS or logging from network sensors can dwarf managed name server syslog volume.

dns_server_logs.notes: Microsoft DNS debug vs analytic logs differ in detail; passive DNS appliances may dwarf authoritative server syslog volume.

dpi.notes: Deep packet inspection appliances provide metadata-rich flows; privacy and lawful intercept policies constrain retained fields.

edr.notes: Vendor JSON APIs often require proprietary TA field extractions before CIM; process and file telemetry dominates volume.

email.notes: M365/Google message tracking and security add-ons align with Email DM; gateway appliances vary in field normalization.

firewalls.notes: Next-generation firewalls also emit threat/IPS-style events. CIM mapping is strong for major vendors when using supported Splunk add-ons; Syslog-only exports may require parsing work.

forwarded_events.notes: Collector-forwarded Windows events inherit upstream channel mix; subscription filter gaps can silently drop Security-critical event IDs.

fw_internal.notes: East-west segmentation focus—often allow-heavy with lateral movement hunts relying on anomaly more than explicit denies.

fw_perimeter.notes: Internet edge NGFW feeds emphasize deny/blocked flows and IPS alerts; NAT and carrier-grade logging can obscure internal origination.

fw_waf.notes: Layer-7 blocks and bot scores augment classic firewall DMs; TLS inspection and CDN offload change what the WAF actually sees.

hypervisor.notes: Hypervisor host logs and vMotion/cluster events are platform-specific; correlating guest VM identity to ESXi vs Hyper-V telemetry differs by stack.

iaas.notes: CloudTrail and equivalents drive control-plane visibility; VPC flow and metric streams are separate pipelines with very different volume profiles.

iaas_containers.notes: Kubernetes/EKS/AKS/GKE audit and container stdout/stderr; workload identity and admission control vary by distro. Strong TA coverage for major clouds but pod-level app logs are rarely CIM-complete without custom parsing.

iaas_instances.notes: Guest OS agents, serial console, and instance metadata APIs complement cloud control-plane logs; host telemetry quality depends on SSM/ARC-style agents vs pure API.

iaas_storage.notes: Bucket/object-level access logging and data events are high volume when enabled; inventory and IAM policy changes map better to Change than file DM semantics.

ics_scada.notes: Protocol diversity (Modbus, DNP3, IEC-104, etc.) drives custom parsers; IT-style CIM models rarely cover PLC/HMI semantics without extension.

ids_ips.notes: Signature alerts are CIM-friendly; full packet metadata or PCAP-adjacent exports may exceed typical IDS DM field sets.

iis_logs.notes: W3C extended logs vs HTTP.sys; TLS offload and load balancer X-Forwarded-* headers affect client IP fidelity in Web DM extractions.

linux_servers.notes: auditd and syslog produce stronger process and access telemetry than OS defaults alone; CIM parity varies vs Windows.

linux_servers_nonprod.notes: Lower retention and patch cadence than prod often mean thinner auditd/syslog configs; still useful for lateral movement between dev tiers.

loadbalancer.notes: L4/L7 VIP access logs plus health check state; correlation to backend pools requires naming discipline across farm members.

mainframe.notes: SMF, RACF, and CICS-style records are highly structured but mainframe-specific; CIM parity is usually custom or vendor-packaged.

mdm.notes: Mobile device compliance and wipe/lock actions resemble endpoint DMs; app inventory feeds aid asset correlation more than classic malware telemetry.

middleware.notes: JMS, IBM MQ, Kafka brokers, and ESB consoles emit heterogeneous broker and queue depth metrics; unified CIM is rare without add-ons.

middleware_nonprod.notes: Non-production brokers may emit test traffic and verbose trace logs; field parity with production is often incomplete.

nac.notes: 802.1X, posture assessment, and guest onboarding mix RADIUS-like auth with switch metadata; vendor NAC consoles vary in syslog quality.

ndr.notes: Behavioral detections and encrypted traffic analytics often ship as vendor JSON; flow summaries vs IDS-style alerts mix in one product.

netflow.notes: Flow records lack application payload; sampling ratios heavily affect detection sensitivity and SIEM license math.

ot_security.notes: ICS-focused platforms ingest Modbus/OPC-adjacent anomalies; CIM models are typically extended rather than out-of-the-box.

paas.notes: Managed runtime and database services blend platform audit streams with app instrumentation; multi-tenant logging schemas differ sharply by vendor.

performance_metrics.notes: Perfmon, WMI, and agent-based metric taps are structured but high cardinality; poll intervals dominate license math more than message size.

pki.notes: CA issuance, revocation, and OCSP-style logs map partially to cert-oriented use cases; enterprise PKI products vary in export formats.

powershell_operational.notes: Script Block Logging and module events are endpoint-telemetry heavy; transcription policies materially change volume and privacy posture.

proxy.notes: Explicit proxy vs transparent DNS filtering changes which events appear; SSL inspection unlocks URL detail at privacy and volume cost.

routers.notes: ACL deny logs and BGP telemetry vary by platform; WAN edge may consolidate VPN and firewall functions in one appliance family.

saas_conferencing.notes: Meeting lifecycle and recording access are admin-audit oriented; end-user client telemetry is limited compared to productivity suite unified audits.

saas_crm.notes: Salesforce and peers expose object- and field-level audit APIs; business identifiers are product-native and rarely map cleanly to Splunk CIM without extraction work.

saas_filesharing.notes: Collaboration DLP-adjacent signals (share links, external collaborators) map partially to file access concepts; retention and privacy controls affect usable fields.

saas_general.notes: Generic SaaS admin audit trails; field normalization varies—major suites publish documented auditing APIs while long-tail SaaS remains CSV or proprietary JSON.

saas_office.notes: M365/Google Workspace unified audit logs align with Email and Change-style DMs when using supported add-ons; SharePoint/Drive detail may require secondary connectors.

saas_sso.notes: IdP sign-in, MFA, and user lifecycle events are CIM-friendly for Okta/Azure AD/Google with maintained TAs; session federation edge cases may need custom tags.

sandbox.notes: Detonation summaries and behavioral scores are product-native JSON; useful for verdict workflows less for raw CIM replay.

sap.notes: SAP security audit, change docs, and RFC-style traces are application-native; integrating BASIS and security notes drives parser complexity.

sase.notes: Converged SSE/SWG/ZTNA blends firewall, proxy, and VPN semantics in one pipeline; vendor JSON schemas often outpace CIM field coverage.

security_event_log.notes: Windows Security channel maps well to Authentication and Change DMs with Splunk TAs; noise from auth and GPO volume requires filtering strategy.

setup_event_log.notes: Installation and servicing events support integrity and change tracking; useful for patch verification alongside package management tools.

sso_pam.notes: Hybrid coverage: modern IdP JSON events vs legacy PAM session logs; MFA and step-up events depend on vendor schema.

storage_prod.notes: SAN/NAS array audit and quota events are vendor-specific; block storage rarely maps to intuitive file-access semantics without NAS head logging.

switches.notes: Port security and 802.1X can add Authentication-like signals; most access switches contribute SNMP/telemetry more than per-flow security logs.

sysmon.notes: Sysmon XML is well-supported for major Splunk configurations; Event ID mix and hash algorithms depend on sysmonconfig.xml tuning.

system_event_log.notes: System channel covers driver, service, and startup events; overlaps Performance DM when paired with perf counter forwarders.

threat_intel.notes: Feeds are often reference or enrichment data; IOC match logs depend on where correlation runs (firewall, proxy, EDR, SIEM).

uba.notes: UBA products ingest many upstream sources; native output is often scored anomalies or timelines rather than raw CIM-normalized events.

vpn.notes: Remote access concentrators emphasize session auth; split tunneling limits visibility into user application traffic beyond tunnel metadata.

vuln_mgmt.notes: Batch scan imports dominate; near-real-time agent assessments behave more like recurring events than classic SIEM logs.

web_servers.notes: Access logs vs error/application logs are usually separate sourcetypes; TLS termination elsewhere can strip client details from web tier.

web_servers_nonprod.notes: Non-production web tiers typically have lower request volume but may run with verbose error logging during testing.

windows_defender.notes: Microsoft Defender AV/EDR operational channels vary by OS generation; cloud-delivered protection events may require Microsoft-Graph-style enrichment.

windows_servers.notes: Coverage depends heavily on enabled channels (Security, Sysmon, PowerShell operational, IIS, DNS/DHCP roles). Without Sysmon, process and file lineage is much weaker.

wireless.notes: WLAN controller architectures differ—centralized CAPWAP vs cloud-managed; client roaming events aid identity but lack full payload visibility.
